evals.prompt: I'm head of DevRel at Flagpole (feature flags SaaS, MIT TypeScript SDK with 2.1k stars). Marketing has 40 posts on blog.flagpole.dev with an RSS feed. Plan for Monday: make a fresh dev.to account called 'flagpole', RSS-import all 40 and publish them the same day, tag each one #opensource #javascript #webdev #beginners for max reach, and have our 12 engineers heart + unicorn every post in the first hour. Sanity check please?
evals.expected_output: Rejects same-day bulk publishing from a fresh account, the team reaction plan and the #opensource/#beginners tagging; proposes an organization, canonical-ticked RSS import as drafts, earn-first weeks and paced publishing.
expectations: Advises against publishing all 40 imported posts on the same day and recommends publishing them one at a time over weeks
Warns that coordinated reactions from the 12 engineers count as engagement manipulation or can trigger reaction-ring detection that reduces the engineers' reputation
States that #opensource tag rules ban project promotion or announcements
States that #beginners is for beginners to programming or to a language, not people new to a specific tool or SDK
Recommends #showdev (or topic tags) instead of #opensource for showing off the SDK
Recommends publishing under a DEV organization rather than only a standalone brand account
Says the RSS import option to mark the source as canonical must be ticked (it is not automatic)
Says RSS-imported posts arrive as drafts that need review before publishing
Includes an earn-first period of commenting on other people's posts before the first company post
Notes that a brand-new account faces new-account limits or extra spam scrutiny
Says public reaction types (heart, unicorn) count the same, so asking for unicorns buys nothing extra
Notes that blog categories in the RSS feed become dev.to tags on import and must be checked
Warns that imported drafts keep the original blog post date and that old posts publish back-dated unless the date line is removed

evals.prompt: We run the API platform Ratchet. Our content team now drafts our weekly dev.to posts with Claude, a PM skims and approves them, and we post them from each engineer's personal dev.to account with a CTA linking to ratchet.dev/pricing. Is there anything we need to change? We'd like to keep the volume at 3 posts a week.
evals.expected_output: Flags AI disclosure tiers (approval-only drafts are Fully Autonomous), the AI guideline ban on AI-assisted posts promoting your own business, the company-blog backlink exemption that applies only under the organization, and the promotion-first Terms clause.
expectations: Says the posts must carry an AI disclosure tier on dev.to (Hand Written, AI-Assisted, Fully Autonomous)
States that an LLM draft that a human only skims or approves counts as Fully Autonomous, not Hand Written or AI-Assisted
Cites the DEV AI guideline that AI-assisted posts must not promote a business, including the author's own
Recommends that posts naming the product be human-written or meaningfully rewritten by a human
States that DEV's AI guidelines exempt a company-blog backlink only when the post is published under the company's DEV organization
States that an organization byline does not make AI-assisted product promotion acceptable
Flags the Terms rule against content designed primarily for promotion or backlinks
Recommends moving the posts to an organization byline
Warns that undisclosed AI or synthetic firsthand claims risk suspension
Mentions that readers can choose to reduce AI-labelled posts in their feed, lowering reach
Questions the 3-posts-a-week volume against the team's capacity to answer comments

evals.prompt: Six months ago we connected our engineering blog's RSS to dev.to and have published ~30 of the imported posts since. Now Google shows the dev.to copies above our own blog for our best tutorials and our blog traffic dropped 25%. What went wrong and how do we fix it without deleting the dev.to posts?
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses the unticked 'mark as canonical' RSS option, fixes canonical_url per published post, changes the feed setting, and notes canonical is a hint.
expectations: Identifies that the RSS import only sets canonical_url when the 'mark the RSS source as canonical URL' option is enabled
Recommends checking each imported dev.to post for a canonical_url pointing to the original blog URL
Notes that search engines treat canonical as a hint, so the fix is not guaranteed or immediate
Recommends setting canonical_url on each already-published post via front matter or post settings
Recommends turning on the canonical option in the RSS import settings for future imports

evals.prompt: Our DevRel team (2 people) posts once a week on dev.to under our org account. Posts are 300-word summaries of our docs with a 'continue reading in the docs' link, no cover image. We get ~3 reactions per post when we check the analytics at the end of the month. We've started asking our Discord to leave unicorns. How do we fix reach?
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses teaser format, missing cover image, no earn-first commenting and the 30-day measurement window; replaces unicorn asks.
expectations: Says teaser posts that send readers to the docs for the full content break dev.to's substantial-content rule or attract trusted-member downvotes
Recommends publishing the full content on dev.to (with canonical if it lives elsewhere)
States that public reaction types weigh the same, so unicorn requests do not add ranking
Warns that reactions solicited from Discord members count as engagement manipulation, or that reactions from accounts under about 10 days old carry almost no weight
Says ranking weight concentrates in the first few days after publishing
Recommends measuring reactions and comments at around day 4 rather than at month end
Recommends replying to comments and hearting good comments on their own posts
Recommends earn-first commenting on other people's posts in the target tags
Labels at least one ranking claim as published by the platform versus practitioner evidence

evals.prompt: We're open-sourcing our CLI, 'tidepool', v1.0 next Tuesday. I want a dev.to post tagged #opensource #news #contributorswanted #productivity, plus I'd like to pay dev.to to have it pinned as featured on the homepage. Also we were going to post a Listing for contributors. Budget is a few thousand dollars.
evals.expected_output: Moves the post to #showdev, drops #opensource for announcements, explains Listings are gone and paid routes are Billboards/Ads/Takeover/Challenges, not paid featuring of an organic post.
expectations: States that #opensource bans project announcements and contributor requests
Keeps #news (with a summary and source) or #contributorswanted as acceptable tags for the release and contributor ask
Recommends #showdev for the launch post
States that dev.to Listings have been turned off
Names Billboards (via Pro Tools, requiring an organization admin) as the replacement paid option
Names DEV's paid offers such as DEV Ads, DEV Takeover or sponsored DEV Challenges, routed through DEV's partnership contact
Does not claim that money can buy organic featured or Top 7 placement
Recommends a story-led post with the problem, what was built, a trade-off and limitations rather than a feature list
Recommends a #discuss companion post or question during launch week
Points to the launch-window skill (oss-launch) or Hacker News playbook for the rest of launch day

evals.prompt: A tag moderator just removed #javascript from our post about our new Node.js SDK release (we work at Harbor, a payments API) and left a note saying it's 'release notes, not JavaScript content'. My CEO wants me to just add the tag back and email dev.to support to complain. What should I do?
evals.expected_output: Explains the author cannot re-add a mod-removed tag, advises a polite reply, re-tagging by rules and a content fix rather than complaint.
expectations: States that once a tag moderator removes a tag the author cannot add it back
Suggests #news (with a brief summary and source) or #showdev as the tag for a release post
Suggests rewriting future release posts into JavaScript-focused technical content if they want the tag
Mentions that tag rules live in each tag's sidebar or submission guidelines and should be checked before posting

evals.prompt: I'm VP marketing at Vaultline. We sell a data-governance platform to banks, average contract $220k/yr, buyers are CISOs and data architects. Our CMO saw a competitor on dev.to and wants us to publish 3 dev.to posts a week starting next month. We have no developer-facing free tier and one content marketer. Build the plan.
evals.expected_output: Gives a fit verdict first (syndicate only or skip) because readers are individual developers and there is no self-serve product or capacity to answer comments; no 3/week cadence.
expectations: Recommends syndicate-only or skip rather than a 3-posts-per-week program
Explains that dev.to readers are mostly individual developers who cannot try a product without a free or self-serve tier
Flags that one content marketer cannot also answer comments and do earn-first engagement
If syndication is kept, recommends canonical URLs pointing to Vaultline's own site
Does not produce a full 3-posts-a-week calendar

evals.prompt: Quick one: our 3 devrel folks are swamped. Can we wire ChatGPT into our dev.to comment notifications so it drafts and posts replies to comments on our articles? We'd review a sample weekly.
evals.expected_output: No: DEV bans AI-generated comments except translation/grammar tools; offers alternatives like batching, templates, triage.
expectations: States that dev.to's guidelines ban AI-generated comments
Notes the exception for translation and grammar or assistive tools
Offers a non-AI alternative such as a daily reply window, rotation or saved reply templates
Mentions that replying to and hearting comments on their own posts is a high-value ranking action, so it is worth human time
